historical_references.reference: Al-Munif was a title given to the righteous caliph 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib by some of his companions due to his generosity and piety.
historical_references.context: During the time of the Rashidun Caliphate, 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib was regarded as a just and merciful ruler. Some of his companions affectionately referred to him as Al-Munif (the generous or bountiful one) due to his charitable nature and piety.

historical_references.reference: Another historical reference for the name 'Munif' can be found in the poetry of Ibn al-Farid (1181-1235 AD), where he uses the term to describe a Sufi master who imparts spiritual knowledge to his disciples.
historical_references.context: In the context of Sufism, the term 'Munif' was used to describe a spiritual guide who revealed the inner truths of the faith to his disciples, often through veiled language and symbolic stories.
